open_issues: Wakeel.Core.Tests.DailyShellPerformanceTests.TheAttentionCenterAndTheBadgesAnswerWithinTheBudgetOn10kRows fails in the full run (wall-clock budget, 200ms) while other agents build in the same tree, and passes when run alone (--filter FullyQualifiedName~DailyShellPerformanceTests: Passed 2, Failed 0). It belongs to the daily-shell package, not to b3-letter. That is the 1 failure in 585.

dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop needed three attempts: a running Wakeel.Desktop.exe (PID 28992) held Wakeel.Core/UI/Design/Reports/Crypto DLLs in its output folder, and one attempt also hit a transient CS0103 'ToggleSort' in src/Wakeel.UI/Pages/W09Overdue.razor (another package's live work). Both cleared on retry; final build is 0 warnings, 0 errors.

ITemplateService.SaveLocalCopyAsync now returns Task<LetterTemplateCheck> instead of Task, and ILetterPdfWriter.ToPdfAsync gained a LetterPageSize parameter (defaulted to A4). No caller exists outside this package today, but the W88/B3 screen packages should pass letter.PageSize and show the returned check when a template is refused.

TemplateService screens the uploaded/local template package only. The letter itself is composed from whatever GetAsync returns, so a local copy the office edits in Word could still gain an attached template; the AutomationSecurity=3 guard in WordSession is what stops anything in it running when الوكيل opens the letter.
notes:
Every high/medium/low finding and all three missing spec items are addressed. Per finding:

(1, high) src/Wakeel.Desktop/Services/LetterPdfWriter.cs was rewritten. It no longer takes Func<CoreWebView2?> and never touches MainWindow.Engine. ThroughWebViewAsync now marshals to the dispatcher and calls PrintOffScreenAsync, which creates a WPF Window that is never shown (Visibility.Hidden, ShowActivated=false, off-screen), takes its HWND with WindowInteropHelper.EnsureHandle, builds its own CoreWebView2Environment with userDataFolder <root>\staging\print, creates a controller with IsVisible=false and page-shaped Bounds, NavigateToString + awaits NavigationCompleted (60s ceiling linked to the caller's token), prints, and closes controller and window in a finally. The Source save/restore is gone. IsAvailable now asks CoreWebView2Environment.GetAvailableBrowserVersionString instead of the window.

(2, medium + supervisor ruling 1) src/Wakeel.Core/Services/CoreAr.cs is now `public static partial class CoreAr` (that one word is the whole diff of the file). LetterAr.cs is deleted; its contents live in src/Wakeel.Core/Services/Correspondence/CoreAr.Letter.cs as `public static partial class CoreAr { public static class Letter { ... } }`, namespace Wakeel.Core.Services. All callers updated (LetterContracts crefs, TemplateService cref, LetterComposer, LetterHtmlRenderer, DerivedDocumentBuilder, and the three test files), with `using Wakeel.Core.Services;` added where needed.

(3, medium + missing spec item 2) ILetterPdfWriter.ToPdfAsync gained `LetterPageSize pageSize = LetterPageSize.A4`. LetterPageLayout.SizeInInches(size) is the pure helper (A4 8.27x11.69, A5 5.85x8.27 — derived from the same twips the docx gets, so the PDF and the Word output are on the same page) and is asserted in LetterPageLayoutTests.The_page_is_also_known_in_the_unit_a_print_job_speaks. LetterPdfWriter.PageSetup sets PageWidth/PageHeight from it, all four margins to 0, ShouldPrintBackgrounds=true, ShouldPrintHeaderAndFooter=false, and that object is what PrintToPdfStreamAsync now receives instead of null.

(4, medium + missing spec item 1) WordSession.Run sets `word.AutomationSecurity = 3` (msoAutomationSecurityForceDisable) immediately after `dynamic word = application;` and before Documents.Open — the only place the package creates Word. TemplateService.IsPlainLetterPackage (System.IO.Compression + XDocument, no new package) refuses: any entry named vbaProject.bin or vbaData.xml; a main part whose declared content type is not application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.main+xml (read from Override AND Default elements — the SDK writes a Default for a minimal package, which is why the first attempt rejected the test fixtures); and any relationship in any .rels part with TargetMode="External" whose type is not /hyperlink. I deliberately exempted hyperlinks: an address or website in a letterhead is written as one and Word follows it only on a click, whereas an attachedTemplate, linked image, OLE object or subdocument is fetched when the file opens. A refused file gets LetterTemplateCheck.Unreadable and therefore the existing CoreAr.Letter.TemplateUnreadable sentence. SaveLocalCopyAsync runs the same check and writes nothing when it fails, returning the check (signature changed from Task to Task<LetterTemplateCheck>). Four new tests cover macros, an attachedTemplate on a share, a macro-enabled main part under a .docx name, and the accepted hyperlink case, with PackageTamper.cs as the fixture builder.

(5, medium) LetterOpenXml.MergeRuns walks paragraph.ChildElements. A non-Run child resets previous/previousProperties unless it is one of the text-free markers (ParagraphProperties, BookmarkStart/End, ProofError, CommentRangeStart/End). New LetterOpenXmlTests proves the hyperlink case does not reorder the line and the bookmark case still merges.

(6, low) LetterHtmlRenderer.FillHtml splits a template line at its mark boundaries: the template's own words are HtmlEncoded outside the bdi, each substituted value is `<bdi>value</bdi>`, an unknown mark is left verbatim, an empty value leaves nothing. AppendBody now receives the raw prefix/suffix plus values and keeps a plain copy for its emptiness checks. The test asserts the concrete `<bdi>و/م/1448/214</bdi>`, `<bdi>19 صفر 1448</bdi>` and that `<bdi>الرقم` does NOT occur; the opening-phrase test now expects `بالإشارة إلى الموضوع أعلاه، <bdi>نأمل الموافقة.</bdi>`.

(7, low) LetterBodyWriter.ApplyListLook sets JustificationValues.Start; Compose_writes_paragraphs_lists_and_bold asserts the list paragraph's justification is not "both" (new LetterProbe.JustificationOf).

(8, low) ReanchorVmlStyle(style, leftMarginTwips, topMarginTwips) now moves the shape as well as re-anchoring it: it finds left/margin-left and top/margin-top, subtracts the margin in the unit the value was written in (pt, in, cm, mm, pc, px), and only then writes :margin. "column" is renamed but never moved. An unreadable distance leaves that axis on the page rather than displacing it. A page-relative axis with no distance at all gets an explicit negative-margin distance, so the A5 invariant "nothing anchored to the paper" still holds. Six theory cases cover this.

(9, low) LetterComposer.Fill records which paragraphs carry LetterMarks.Body BEFORE the simple values are substituted, then inserts once into each. That kills both the loop and the data-driven variant: a subject or an editor line quoting the mark can no longer receive the body. LetterBodyWriter.Insert returns the last paragraph it produced. New test Compose_never_pours_the_letter_into_its_own_words.

(10, low) LetterNumbering uses LevelText "" with the Symbol RunFonts, and inserts the two abstract definitions after the last w:numPicBullet (PrependChild only when there is none). TemplateBuilder.WithPictureBullet + Compose_leaves_a_template_s_picture_bullets_in_front_of_its_own_definitions assert the part order; the bullet character is asserted in the list test.

(11, low) xunit here is 2.9.3, so Assert.Skip does not exist and no skippable-fact package is pinned. I added tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests/Letters/WordFacts.cs with [WordFact] and [NoWordFact] (FactAttribute subclasses that set Skip at discovery). The run summary now prints "Skipped: 1" with the Arabic reason instead of a silently green no-op; on this machine the real Word test ran and passed.

Build/test line, run exactly as specified and read in full: dotnet build src/Wakeel.Reports — 0/0. dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core — 0/0. dotnet build tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests --no-dependencies — 0/0. dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests --no-build — Failed 1, Passed 583, Skipped 1, Total 585 (the 1 is the daily-shell performance budget; see open_issues; the letter package's own 101 tests pass and 1 skips with its reason). dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop — 0 warnings, 0 errors (third attempt; file locks and another package's transient razor error, see open_issues). TreatWarningsAsErrors is clean everywhere, no NuGet package was added, and Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Wakeel.slnx and docs/ (bar the progress file) are untouched.
